mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals a broad-based fall in economic activity, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise above their respective 12-month averages simultaneously, it signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average while UNRATE remains below 4.0% for three months suggests labor market expansion without wage inflation, supporting corporate margins and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12mo avg AND UNRATE < 4.0% for three months
regime_hint: labor market expansion with stable wages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly increases in RSAFS and subsequent S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as rising household savings can signal anticipated future consumption and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS increases and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.
